justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Among the best-evidenced upper extremity rehab interventions post-stroke and for pediatric hemiplegia. EXCITE trial landmark.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: Multi-day CIMT training plus constrained practice requires dedicated equipment and space; moderate investment.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Limited to stroke patients with residual upper limb function; requires intensive format not feasible in most settings.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Billed as intensive OT/PT; commercial payers cover at standard therapy rates; frequency justification often required.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Moderate demand in neuro specialty programs and stroke rehabilitation centers.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Restraint tolerated when motivation high; pediatric populations show high family engagement.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Stroke/neuro families will pay for intensive programs, but population is narrower and often insurance/Medicare-driven.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Intensive protocol model supports package pricing in niche neuro clinics.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Relatively few certified providers; defensible neuro niche.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Protocol-based — can train staff to deliver, but volume is limited by patient pool.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Stroke survivors/families do search for it, but a small subsegment.
justifications.business.efficiency: Multi-day training, moderate cost; delivery is labor-intensive (massed practice).
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Strong neuro credential aligning with NCS faculty profiles.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Taub's body of work and ongoing RCTs make this a publishable, fundable area.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Core example in neuro rehab curricula for motor learning and neuroplasticity.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: EXCITE trial and multiple systematic reviews — among the best-evidenced neuro interventions.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Useful but not required; neuro faculty lines lean on NCS more.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Time-intensive training relative to alternatives like NDT or task-specific training coursework.
